conviction_note: Small positive lean: the Fed hiked on 2026-09-16 rather than in December as Schwab's July outlook assumed, so the Q4 NIM guide (3.25-3.30%) has room to move up, the published Q3 activity (record core NNA, margin balances +58% YTD) is strong, and the stock fell 9% in 20 days on an AI-agent narrative while EPS estimates were revised up. Against that, Schwab sold its Q2 beat-and-raise (-2.5% on the day) and the year-end rate level is still inside the guide, so p_up is held at 55; the findings sum to +1.0 and the scaled number is 0.4 because the sign is near a coin flip while the move is not small.
bar: Q3 2026 consensus EPS $1.66 (Zacks via Yahoo, https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/exploring-analyst-estimates-charles-schwab-121503932.html) / $1.67 (Benzinga); revenue $7.19-7.21bn (same two sources); consensus NII $3.57bn, DATs 10.48M (Zacks). Company guide: FY2026 revenue growth 17.5-18.5%, FY NIM 3.00-3.10%, Q4 NIM 3.25-3.30%, assuming one 25bp hike in December and ~13% market appreciation (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/07/21/schwab-schw-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/). Two estimate sources agree within $0.01, so the bar is treated as sourced.
positioning_check: Short interest 1.1% of free float, up ~18% in shares over the past month, borrow cost below 0.5% (ORTEX, 2026-10-12, https://ortex.news/articles/185233/schwab-heads-into-q3-print-with-analysts-split-on-rate-recovery); earlier FINRA reading 16.9M shares, 2.5 days to cover at 2026-08-14 settlement (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/schw/short-interest/ via search snippet). Not crowded. Baseline skew_25d -0.23 vol points (balanced), put/call OI 0.89, event-implied move 3.78%.

findings.finding: The FOMC raised the funds rate 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16, a quarter earlier than the single December hike Schwab's July outlook assumed; at Schwab's own sensitivity of ~$250-300m annualised NII per 25bp that is roughly $60-75m of extra Q4 NII (about 5-6bp of NIM on ~$460bn of interest-earning assets), so the Q4 NIM guide of 3.25-3.30% and the FY revenue guide have room to be raised at the Fall Business Update.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-07-21): FY revenue guide raised to 17.5-18.5% with a beat and the stock fell ~2.5% on the day (https://qz.com/charles-schwab-record-revenue-earnings-retail-trading-072226). Raised guidance has not been bought on this name in 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: The hike is public and estimates moved up modestly (Zacks: EPS consensus +0.4% over 30 days; ORTEX EPS revision momentum 79th percentile), but the stock fell ~9% over the same 20 days rather than rerating on the rate path, so a formally raised Q4 NIM/FY guide is not visible in the price. If it were priced the stock would have held its pre-hike level near $107 instead of $95.62. Partly priced: the year-end rate level (4.00% upper bound) is the one the guide already assumed, so only the timing is new.
findings.independence: Schwab's own rate sensitivity and the July NIM guide are from the Q2 call transcript (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/07/21/schwab-schw-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/); Yahoo/TIKR 2026-09-23 restates the $250-300m per 25bp figure (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/charles-schwab-stock-fell-6-152211144.html).

findings.finding: Schwab's own monthly reports put Q3 core net new assets at $122.9bn for July+August alone ($58.1bn July record, $64.8bn August record, +46% y/y) against $119.8bn for all of Q2, with margin balances at a record $177.6bn (+58% YTD) and sweep cash rebuilding $6.5bn in August to $483.3bn.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Record NNA and record revenue in Q2 were sold (-2.5%, Quartz); Q1 2026 record EPS met a revenue/NII shortfall and fell (reports range from -0.4% to -5%: https://www.tikr.com/blog/charles-schwab-posted-record-q1-2026-earnings-why-did-the-stock-fall).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: these are Schwab's own published monthly numbers and the NII consensus ($3.57bn, +6% q/q) already reflects higher margin and interest-earning assets. What may not be in consensus is the full-quarter average margin balance; if it were fully in, the Zacks NII estimate would imply more than the ~3.10% NIM it does.
findings.independence: July report (https://pressroom.aboutschwab.com/press-releases/press-release/2026/Schwab-Reports-Monthly-Activity-Highlights-f6515f5a5/default.aspx) is a separate document from the August one; IBKR September margin loans +4% m/m to $105.2bn (https://fxnewsgroup.com/forex-news/retail-forex/interactive-brokers-registers-6-y-y-increase-in-darts-in-sep-2026/) points the same way for September.

findings.finding: Trading activity is tracking slightly under the 10.48M DAT consensus: Schwab printed 11.6M in July and 9.8M in August, and Interactive Brokers' September DARTs fell 4% m/m, which implies a Schwab September near 9.4-9.6M and a Q3 average around 10.3M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean history on a DAT miss alone; Q1 2026 was sold on a revenue line shortfall (https://www.tikr.com/blog/charles-schwab-posted-record-q1-2026-earnings-why-did-the-stock-fall).
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus DATs (10.48M, Zacks) sit above the July-August run rate extended by the IBKR September slowdown; if the slowdown were priced the DAT estimate would be near 10.3M. The management guide (FY DATs up to 10.6M with a summer pullback) means a small shortfall is inside what Schwab told the market to expect, and trading is ~16% of revenue, so the size is small. Proxy for September.
findings.independence: Schwab July/August DATs from its own monthly reports (https://www.financialcontent.com/article/bizwire-2026-9-15-schwab-reports-monthly-activity-highlights); the September leg is an IBKR proxy only.

findings.finding: Morgan Stanley's Q3 release (2026-10-14), the first large wealth peer to report after Schwab last spoke, shows wealth NII up to $2.23bn from $1.99bn driven by lending growth and higher average sweep deposits, i.e. no sign that the September hike set off cash sorting out of sweep in the quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Cash-sorting fear was the 2023 bear case; the 2026-09-22 selloff was partly attributed to rate-sensitive brokerage economics (https://www.quiverquant.com/news/Charles+Schwab+Falls+as+Investors+Reassess+Rate-Sensitive+Brokerage+Economics). No print reaction to cite on this line in 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: Released the day before Schwab's print; Schwab's Q3 preview coverage (ORTEX 10-12) still frames the print as a test of cash-sorting fears. If the market had taken the read-through, SCHW would not be sitting at its 20-day low going into the print. Proxy: a different client base (advisor-led, wealthier).
findings.independence: Schwab's own August sweep cash rebuild (+$6.5bn, https://www.financialcontent.com/article/bizwire-2026-9-15-schwab-reports-monthly-activity-highlights) points the same way, but that is pre-hike.

findings.finding: The 20-day drawdown has a named non-earnings cause: SCHW fell 6.1% on 2026-09-22 on fears that AI agents (Meta's Muse, Altruist's planning agent) erode brokerage loyalty, while Q3 EPS estimates were revised up, so the stock enters the print on a compressed multiple rather than on lowered numbers, and the Fall Business Update gives management a platform to answer it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 came after a run-up and the beat was sold (-2.5%); this setup is the reverse (-9.1% 20d, -15.9% from 52w high), so the Q2 reaction is a weak guide.
findings.why_not_priced: The decline is priced by definition; what is not priced is that the fundamental bar moved the other way (EPS consensus +0.4% in 30 days, Zacks; Morgan Stanley target raised to $141 on 10-09). If the market had judged earnings to be at risk, estimates would have been cut alongside the price. A quarterly print does not settle an AI-disintermediation worry, which is why this is small.
findings.independence: Same day reported separately by ad-hoc-news (https://www.ad-hoc-news.de/boerse/news/corporate-news/charles-schwab-stock-falls-6-1-percent-as-ai-risk-hits-brokers/70165523); estimate revision data from Zacks via Yahoo (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/exploring-analyst-estimates-charles-schwab-121503932.html).

baseline_tension: Skew is balanced (-0.23) and the lean is mildly positive against a -9.1% 20-day run-up, so it leans against the recent tape without fighting the option market; the main counterweight is the name's habit of selling good prints in 2026.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (inside the guide): the September hike leaves the year-end funds rate at the 4.00% upper bound the July guide already assumed, so only the timing is new; guidance finding cut from +0.8 to +0.5.
Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): Schwab sold its Q2 beat-and-raise (-2.5%), so the published-activity finding was cut from +0.3 to +0.2 and p_up moved from 56 to 55.
Rule 5 (proxy vs absence of cause): the drawdown has a named cause, so the positioning finding stands, but it is inference about a reaction and was cut from +0.4 to +0.3.
Rule 5 / rule 7: the IBKR and Morgan Stanley proxies were already small and stay as filed; short interest checked (1.1% of float), so the one negative is not shrunk for a squeeze.
Lesson on untrusted history: the base rate was rebuilt from cited same-day reactions (Q2 -2.5%, Q1 -0.4% to -5%), not the sealed history; abs_move_pct stays 4.0.
